tonight.headline: 97.2–56.9 and they have two Rams left on Monday night.
body: Josh Allen's 40.8 on Thursday and Garrett Wilson's 16.7 have carried this. Panda Attack's week broke the other way: Saquon Barkley left with a stinger and came back for 3.0, Javonte Williams is on 2.5, and their 22.5 from Dalton Kincaid is sitting on their bench.

You have Isaiah Likely left on Monday night. They have Davante Adams and Harrison Mevis, both Rams, in the same game. ESPN still only gives you 71% because three of their starters are mid-game in Dallas. There is nothing you can do about any of it — every Chem player you own except Likely is locked.

case.label: The script that beats you
case.body: Their two live players are both Rams at home on Monday night, and Los Angeles are not on the Giants' side of a shootout by reputation — Legendary Upside's Monday preview calls the Rams pass rush 'anemic' and notes they did not blitz against San Francisco. A high-scoring Rams win is the one shape that gets Adams and Mevis to roughly 40 between them, and that is what they need.

case.label: What you actually control
case.body: Nothing in the lineup. Pitts played and scored 2.5, so even the tight end seat is frozen until rosters unlock. The two things worth doing are both waiver claims that clear Wednesday at 01:00 your time, and they are the two cards below.

case.label: What would change it
case.body: Likely getting nothing on Monday while Adams goes for 25-plus. Likely ran a 68% route share in Week 1 with Jaxson Dart at a 134.2 rating, so the floor is not zero, but a single primetime game is the only variance left in this matchup.

doFirst.title: Claim Rashod Bateman, drop Kyle Pitts
doFirst.subtitle: Same seat as this morning's card, different Raven. Bateman went 7-of-9 for 88 and a touchdown. Andrews, the man the card named for four runs, went 6-of-7 for 49.

case.label: The receiver
case.body: Nine targets, seven catches, 88 yards and a touchdown at New Orleans with Zay Flowers out (NBC Sports, today). Baltimore are also without Ja'Kobi Lane, who fractured a wrist, and Devontez Walker with a groin, so the room is three receivers short with Lamar Jackson throwing. His ownership moved +8.02 in a day — the largest single move anywhere on this board — and ESPN's own band flags him MONEY, low owned and rising, at 24.2% rostered here.

case.label: Why not Andrews
case.body: The morning card's argument was that Andrews 'stands first in line for the leftover work'. The box score says the leftover work went outside, not inside: Bateman nine targets to Andrews's seven, 88 yards to 49, and the touchdown. Andrews is also a tight end, and Chem's flex is RB/WR only — behind Isaiah Likely he could never have entered this lineup. Bateman can.

case.label: The drop, and the honest counter
case.body: Pitts cannot enter the RB/WR flex in any week this season and sits behind Likely at tight end, so the seat is structurally dead — STRATEGY section 9 says do not carry a second tight end in Chem. Cooper Rush started a second straight game today and Pitts managed 2.5. The counter, stated rather than buried: NFL Network and ESPN both reported today that Michael Penix Jr. could make his first 2026 start in Week 3 on Thursday night against Green Bay, with Tua Tagovailoa back as his backup. The quarterback half of the Pitts case may expire this week. The structural half does not.

case.label: The price, and the queue
case.body: Chem priority resets weekly, so this claim costs nothing lasting — STRATEGY section 6 says be aggressive here. But AVIATO's waiverRank in this league is 10 of 10, last in the queue. At 24.2% rostered Bateman is the kind of name nobody else claims, which is precisely why he is the safe one to run from the back of the line.

case.label: Falsified if
case.body: Zay Flowers is active in Week 3 and Bateman's target share falls back under 15%. Ian Rapoport had Flowers day-to-day on 14 September and that is the live risk, not Baltimore's volume. Also falsified if Baltimore keep running the ball — 37 carries to 25 pass attempts in Week 1 — in which case one nine-target game with two receivers out was the game script, and Pitts was worth more as a trade chip at 93% rostered.

doFirst.sources: NBC Sports · Yahoo Sports · NFL.com · ESPN · AtlantaFalcons.com

doFirst.title: Claim the Lions D/ST, drop the Ravens
doFirst.subtitle: Ten consecutive runs said hold. This is the first one where the board disagrees: Detroit 3rd for Week 3, Baltimore 16th at Dallas.

case.label: The board turned
case.body: Draft Sharks' Week 3 defence rankings, fetched this run: Carolina 1st at Cleveland, the Giants 2nd against Tennessee, Detroit 3rd hosting the Jets, Green Bay 6th, New England 9th at Jacksonville, Cleveland 14th, Baltimore 16th at Dallas, Chicago 17th. For ten runs Baltimore sat 3rd of 32 on FantasyPros and nothing free here was close. That is no longer true.

case.label: What happened today
case.body: Baltimore lost to New Orleans and the defence scored 3.0, seventh of the eight defences rostered in this league and behind San Francisco's 9.0 and Pittsburgh's 8.0. The hold thesis's own first clause was Baltimore finishing outside the top twelve in Week 2. It tripped.

case.label: The seat, and the rule it bumps into
case.body: This seat last changed hands on 16 September at 07:14, so STRATEGY section 3's seven-day rule technically closes it until 07:14 Wednesday — fourteen minutes after this claim would clear. Section 5 says kicker and D/ST are streamed weekly on matchup without sentiment and requires this comparison every run. I take section 5 as governing the two streamed seats, and note the conflict rather than pretending it is not there. The gap is 3rd against 16th, not a 0.3-point stream.

case.label: What it costs
case.body: Nothing lasting. Priority resets weekly here. Detroit are 51.8% rostered nationally, though, and you claim from waiverRank 10 of 10, so this one is genuinely contestable. Losing it leaves Baltimore in the seat, which is a 16th-ranked draw rather than a disaster.

case.label: Falsified if
case.body: Baltimore outscore Detroit in Week 3 — Dallas have been generous and the Jets are not automatic. Also falsified if New York name a quarterback change that lifts the Jets' offence before Sunday, which would flatten Detroit's draw. The Patriots at 9th and 65.6% rostered are the fallback if the Detroit claim is beaten.

action.label: Claim Lions D/ST · drop Ravens D/ST

doFirst.deadlineLabel: Fallback only · when the week rolls
doFirst.title: Jalen Coker for Terry McLaurin in the flex — unarmed, one clause short
doFirst.subtitle: Coker went 8 for 66 at Atlanta. McLaurin is on 3.4 in a game still running, and his target count is the half of the clause I cannot see from here.

case.label: The half that fired
case.body: The 18 September comparison set two conditions for the flex changing hands. Coker's has fired: 8 catches for 66 yards at Atlanta today, after 8 catches in Week 1. NBC Sports carry the line. He also went full in practice on Friday and came off Carolina's injury report entirely.

case.label: The half that has not
case.body: McLaurin's condition is fewer than six targets at Dallas. Washington are still playing as this is written and he is on 3.4, but the target count is not in the snapshot and a points total is not a target count. Context that matters either way: Washington's offensive coordinator David Blough said the plan was to get McLaurin ten targets a game, and he drew four in Week 1 against Philadelphia (SI, 15 September).

case.label: Why this is unarmed
case.body: Firing a flex change on half a clause is the churn STRATEGY section 3 exists to stop, and there is no legal lineup move today anyway — every Chem player except Likely is locked. This renders unarmed so the comparison is on the record rather than rediscovered on Tuesday.

case.label: What would change it
case.body: McLaurin's final target count at Dallas. Under six and this is a straight swap the moment rosters unlock, on two straight weeks of the target share disagreeing with the route share. Six or more and the 92.1% route participation was the better instrument, the row closes, and Coker stays a bench receiver worth keeping.

whatWentWrong.title: The Flowers-vacancy card named the wrong Raven, four runs running
whatWentWrong.lead: Bateman took nine targets for 7/88/1. Andrews took seven for 6/49/0. The card that has been on your board since 19 September pointed at the tight end.

case.label: What went in
case.body: DraftKings Network on 18 September had Flowers and Andrews each at 25% of Baltimore's Week 1 targets and called Andrews 'the tight end who stands first in line for the leftover work'. With Flowers ruled out, that read made Andrews the buy. It was a reasonable inference from a real number.

case.label: What actually happened
case.body: The leftover work went outside. Bateman nine targets, seven catches, 88 yards, a touchdown. Andrews six catches on seven targets for 49 and no score. In full PPR that is roughly 21.8 to 10.9 — the gap is not a rounding error.

case.label: It was written down in advance
case.body: This morning's Bateman row carried the clause 'seven or more and Andrews is the weaker half of the pair, and Bateman is a free claim on Tuesday since Chem priority resets weekly'. Nine targets. The clause fired exactly as written, which is the whole point of writing it before the game.

case.label: What would change it
case.body: Flowers returning healthy in Week 3. Bateman's 24.2% ownership says the wider market has not yet priced one game, and one game with two receivers out is what this is.

whatWentWrong.sources: NBC Sports · DraftKings Network · Yahoo Sports

whatWentWrong.title: Your defence was held for ten consecutive runs and finished 3.0
whatWentWrong.lead: Baltimore lost to New Orleans. The D/ST scored 3.0, seventh of eight defences rostered in this league, and they draw Dallas next.

case.label: The hold was well-argued and still wrong this week
case.body: FantasyPros had Baltimore 3rd of 32 against a New Orleans line that gave up five first-half sacks in Week 1. Nothing free on this wire was close — the best was New England at 8th. On the information available at 13:05 the hold was right.

case.label: The clause that tripped
case.body: The thesis said 'Baltimore finish outside the top 12 defensive scores in Week 2 while San Francisco finish top 5'. Half of that is confirmed from the league file: Baltimore 3.0, San Francisco 9.0 and top of the eight rostered here. I cannot confirm the top-five cut league-wide from this snapshot, so the second half stays open.

case.label: What it changes
case.body: It fires the D/ST card above. Detroit are 3rd for Week 3 against the Jets on Draft Sharks' board and sit on this wire at 51.8% rostered. This is the streaming decision section 5 asks for every week, and it is the first week the answer is not hold.

case.label: What would change it
case.body: Baltimore beating Detroit's Week 3 output at Dallas. If that happens the churn cost a roster move and the ten-run hold was right all along.

whatWentWrong.title: Your flex scored 3.4 and the receiver you benched scored 14.6
whatWentWrong.lead: Terry McLaurin is on 3.4 with Washington still playing at Dallas. Jalen Coker went 8 for 66 at Atlanta from your bench.

case.label: Why McLaurin was in the flex
case.body: 92.1% route participation in Week 1, highest on Washington, against Diggs at 65.8%. He was off Washington's Week 2 injury report entirely and Jayden Daniels took every snap in Week 1. Route share is the right instrument and it said McLaurin.

case.label: Why it did not pay
case.body: Route share is not target share. McLaurin drew four targets in Week 1 for two catches and 14 yards, and Dan Quinn's own account was that Philadelphia set out to take away the deep ball. Coker meanwhile has cleared eight catches in both weeks with Bryce Young throwing.

case.label: What it changes
case.body: It arms the ghost card above with one of its two clauses. It does not change the lineup today — both players are locked — and it does not on its own reverse a call made on the best available evidence two days ago.

case.label: What would change it
case.body: McLaurin's final target count at Dallas. Six or more and this row is one bad afternoon rather than a role read, and the flex does not move.

worthALook.name: Khalil Shakir
worthALook.lead: Six targets against Detroit on Thursday, which is the number his own clause was waiting on.

case.label: The clause that fired
case.body: The 18 September row said 'six or more makes him a free claim on Wednesday 23 Sep'. NBC Sports headlined his Thursday night 'Modest production for Khalil Shakir on six looks' — three catches, 49 all-purpose yards, six targets. The role is there; the production was not.

case.label: Why he is not a card
case.body: The drop would be Monangai or Brian Thomas Jr., and both had a defensible Sunday: Monangai led Chicago's rushing with Swift fumbling, Thomas was shadowed by Surtain and still cleared 7.0. Claiming a third receiver to bench one of them is exactly the one-slot-three-players churn STRATEGY section 3 names. Two claims are already going in this week.

case.label: When to act
case.body: Wednesday 23 September if Buffalo's Week 3 target distribution holds at six-plus for Shakir and either Monangai loses the Chicago backfield to a healthy Swift or Thomas's target share stays under 18% through Week 3 — Thomas's own written clause. Chem priority resets, so the claim is free whenever it is right.

worthALook.name: Mark Andrews
worthALook.lead: Demoted from a Do-first card to a watch row by his own box score.

case.label: The number that demoted him
case.body: Six catches on seven targets for 49 yards and no touchdown at New Orleans, against Bateman's nine targets and 7/88/1 in the same game. The premise of four runs of cards was that Andrews inherits Flowers's work inside. He did not.

case.label: Why the row survives at all
case.body: 82.4% rostered nationally and still available here, which is the why=OWNED band. Seven targets is a real role and Baltimore are short three receivers. He is a fine tight end — he is just not the right claim for a roster whose flex is RB/WR and whose TE1 ran a 68% route share in Week 1.

case.label: What would change it
case.body: Isaiah Likely appearing on a Giants injury report, which would make a second startable tight end necessary rather than structurally dead. Or Andrews clearing nine targets in Week 3 at Dallas while Bateman falls back, which would say today was the anomaly and reverse the pair.

worthALook.name: Jakobi Meyers
worthALook.lead: Still the largest receiver ownership anomaly here, and still unresolved — his Denver line is not in this snapshot.

case.label: The role
case.body: 182.4 season projection, the highest of any receiver on this wire, at 76.5% rostered nationally. NBC Sports had the thumb cleared and he was active at Denver, with Riley Moss on him while Surtain took Brian Thomas Jr. — the softer half of Denver's coverage.

case.label: Why it is still open
case.body: Jacksonville kicked at 20:05 UTC and no recap carrying his target count had published when this was written. He is a wire player, so the league file carries no actual for him. Four searches produced availability notes and no box score. That is the honest state of it.

case.label: When to act
case.body: Wednesday 23 September if Meyers out-targeted Thomas at Denver — that is Thomas's own thesis breaking and Meyers is the replacement, one-for-one, no new seat. If Thomas won the target count this row closes and Meyers comes off the list for good.

doNotChase.name: Jordan Addison
doNotChase.lead: The ownership anomaly resolved itself downward: 1.6 points with Carson Wentz throwing.

case.label: The number that kills it
case.body: 1.6 in Week 2. Kyler Murray is in concussion protocol and Wentz started again; Minnesota are also without Jauan Jennings, which thins the offence rather than the competition for targets. The 171.4 season projection is describing a quarterback who is not playing.

case.label: Why the number looked good
case.body: 74.9% rostered nationally, dropped inside this league by JuiceJam on 16 September — the why=OWNED band STRATEGY section 4 ranks as the strongest single wire signal. It is the right signal pointed at the wrong cause: he is free here because his quarterback changed, not because a manager blundered.

case.label: What would change it
case.body: Murray clearing protocol for Week 3. Chem priority resets weekly, so he would be cheap to claim the moment that happens and there is no cost to waiting for it.

doNotChase.name: Rachaad White
doNotChase.lead: Top why=OWNED back on this wire and the second back in his own backfield.

case.label: The number that kills it
case.body: Washington's Week 1 backfield snaps: Jacory Croskey-Merritt 33, White 27, Kaytron Allen 6 of 67. Croskey-Merritt scored 3.6 today and White's own line is still mid-game at Dallas. A committee back who is second in his own committee is the flex body section 4 calls a bad add.

case.label: Why the number looks good
case.body: 164.6 season projection and 65.4% national ownership, both describing the job he had in Tampa. His ownership is drifting down, not up — -0.73 on the day.

case.label: What would change it
case.body: Croskey-Merritt missing a game, or White clearing five targets in a week. He is also Team 13's second starting running back in IPADE, which is what makes the Lamar Jackson offer there work; if he is dropped or benched over there, that trade loses its 'their gain' number.

doNotChase.name: Xavier Worthy
doNotChase.lead: A free agent at 74.7% rostered, and Kansas City are still throwing for 184 yards a game.

case.label: The number that kills it
case.body: Kansas City threw for 184 team yards in Week 1 and Pro Football Network's Week 2 piece on him is headlined 'Close to a Cut'. Rashee Rice is entirely off the Week 2 injury report, so the vacancy that would make Worthy matter does not exist.

case.label: Why the number looks good
case.body: 173.9 season projection and a free agent here at 74.7% national ownership, which reads as a blunder by somebody. It is not: he is priced on a passing volume Kansas City have not produced.

case.label: What would change it
case.body: Kansas City's air-yards profile normalising over two weeks, or Rice missing time. They play Indianapolis tonight with Mahomes throwing and Daniel Jones on the other side, so both branches get a data point in a few hours and neither is in this snapshot.

cannotSee.label: Season projections are frozen, and this run measured it
cannotSee.body: I pulled the 15:07Z copy of a league file from the repository's commit history and compared it against the current one: 251 players, and not one seasonProj moved, while twelve weekly projections did. seasonProj is a preseason artifact. Every trade priced on it — including the two standing IPADE offers — is trading on August's opinion, and Chem's own zero-mutual-gain trade result rests on the same frozen number.

cannotSee.label: The Rams against tight ends is not researched
cannotSee.body: Isaiah Likely's tile is dashed. Two searches for a Rams points-allowed-to-TE rank returned season-long aggregate pages I could not read a 2026 figure out of. What I do have is usage: 68% route participation and 8/78/2 in Week 1, and a Monday preview calling the Rams' pass rush anemic. That is a usage read, not a matchup grade, and I am not dressing it up as one.

cannotSee.label: No Week 3 kicker board by name
cannotSee.body: Draft Sharks' Week 3 kicker table came back as team abbreviations with the name column missing: Atlanta 3rd, San Francisco 4th, Chicago 6th, Seattle 9th, Baltimore 17th. That is enough to say Loop's draw is mediocre and not enough to name a replacement with confidence, which is why the kicker seat is held rather than streamed alongside the defence.

cannotSee.body: Both cards above are claims, and AVIATO is last in this week's queue. Bateman at 24.2% rostered is very unlikely to be contested. The Lions at 51.8% genuinely can be. Priority resets weekly here so losing either costs nothing but the week.

cannotSee.label: Rivals' pending claims are invisible
cannotSee.body: ESPN returns only your own pending waiver claims. Nine other managers watched the same Bateman and Detroit lines this afternoon and I cannot see whether any of them have already put a claim in.

cannotSee.label: Week 3 opponents are not in the league file
cannotSee.body: proTeams carries this week's matchup only. Every Week 3 statement in this brief — Baltimore at Dallas, Detroit against the Jets, Atlanta at Green Bay on Thursday — comes from outside sources, not from the snapshot, and is as good as those sources.

cannotSee.body: Two games of points-allowed is not a sample. The Detroit-over-Baltimore call rests on one publisher's Week 3 board plus a Baltimore result, which is a thinner base than the ten-run hold it reverses.

cannotSee.body: Second consecutive run in which a page returned by an explicit 2026 query described a different season. This league's rosters diverge from the obvious ones — Likely is a Giant, Dowdle a Steeler, Meyers a Jaguar, Rachaad White a Commander — so a familiar name on a familiar team is the failure mode. Every claim above was cross-checked against the league file's team assignment.
